content.value_statement: Belgian healthcare practices must manage convention decisions, patient notices, and changing reimbursement procedures. This guide helps AI assistants draft administrative briefings and checklists for professional review.
actual_capabilities: Guides drafting convention versus de-convention financial briefings for dentists, physiotherapists, and speech therapists.
Guides drafting patient notices about convention status, supplements, and reimbursement changes.
Supports tariff poster drafts for review against applicable display requirements.
Outlines patient intake structures covering eHealth consent and insurance status.
Guides administrative checklists for eAttest, eFact, and third-party payer workflows.
limitations: The supplied folder contains only a public guide, without the original scripts, extension source, or templates.
No live integration, submission mechanism, or automatic regulatory update process is supplied.
The guide asserts 2026 reimbursement rules without official citations; current requirements and financial assumptions need independent verification.
The scope excludes medical advice, diagnosis, and clinical nomenclature selection; generated documents do not guarantee legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Compare Convention Options
use_cases.description: Prepare a convention status briefing using aggregate patient mix, verified reimbursement assumptions, and estimated premium changes.

use_cases.title: Organize Digital Attestation Tasks
use_cases.description: Draft an eAttest and eFact checklist with staff responsibilities and unresolved requirements for verification.

use_cases.title: Prepare Patient Communications
use_cases.description: Draft tariff posters and patient notices using supplied fees, convention status, and effective dates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an administrative checklist for a Belgian [discipline] practice using [eAttest or eFact]. Mark requirements that need official verification.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Patient Notice
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Dutch patient notice about [fee change]. Use [convention status], [effective date], and [verified amounts]. Leave unknown reimbursement figures blank.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Tariff Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Dutch tariff poster for [discipline] using [approved fee table], [convention status], and [effective date]. List display requirements needing professional review.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Financial Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare convention options for [discipline] using [aggregate patient mix], [volumes], [fees], [verified reimbursement rules], and [premium changes]. Show assumptions and sensitivity scenarios. Identify missing evidence.

output_examples.input: Draft a de-convention briefing for a speech therapist with 30% increased-reimbursement patients, without verified tariff data.
output: Patient mix: 30% increased reimbursement and 70% other patients.
Financial comparison remains incomplete until current fees, reimbursement rules, and premium changes are verified.
Review separate patient-group scenarios and prepare updated notices after the decision.

output_examples.input: Outline an eAttest readiness checklist for a dental practice.
output: Confirm applicable obligations and effective dates using official guidance.
Review patient identification, insurance status, and relevant consent handling.
Assign submission, rejection follow-up, and reconciliation responsibilities.
Verify the workflow in the practice software before operational use.

best_practices: Verify dates, reimbursement rules, and display obligations against current official RIZIV/INAMI guidance before using drafts.
Use anonymized examples or aggregate patient statistics instead of identifiable patient records.
Have a qualified practice administrator or adviser review financial assumptions and patient-facing documents.
anti_patterns: Treating the guide's 2026 statements as verified current law without checking official sources.
Expecting the guide to submit attestations or operate ProGezondheid and practice software automatically.
Using administrative drafts for diagnosis, medical advice, or clinical nomenclature selection.

faq.question: Which practices does this guide address?
faq.answer: It focuses on Belgian dentists, physiotherapists, and speech therapists handling RIZIV/INAMI administration.

faq.question: Does it connect to eAttest or eFact?
faq.answer: No live integration is supplied. The guide supports drafting workflow checklists, not submitting attestations or claims.

faq.question: Are its 2026 reimbursement claims verified?
faq.answer: The supplied guide gives no official citations for those claims. Confirm current rules with RIZIV/INAMI before making decisions.

faq.question: Can it produce legally compliant tariff posters?
faq.answer: It can guide poster drafts, but compliance is not guaranteed. Check required content, fees, and display obligations before publication.

faq.question: Can I use it for clinical advice?
faq.answer: No. Its stated scope excludes medical advice, diagnosis, and clinical nomenclature selection.

faq.question: Does this folder include the original automation package?
faq.answer: No. It contains a public SKILL.md guide; the original scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
